 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of B.N.Kemparaju caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 24.08.2020 at SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.3272/2020 about 4.00 pm., when B.N.Kemparaju (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was riding his Honda Shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-L-6060 from Dabaspete to Nelamangala on Tumkur-Bangalore NH-48 on the Billinakote bridge slowly, carefully by observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time, a Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life while crossing the divider and dashed to the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and the said Innova car dashed to the another two more cars and others also sustained injuries.

Immediately deceased was taken to Swastya Hospital,
Nelamangala and in the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 29.08.2020.

3. Further it is the case of the Petitioners that prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 28 years, he was a Sales Executive in SLN Insurance Company, Arishinakunte,
Nelamangala and earning Rs.70,000/- per month.
Due to his death, SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.3272/2020 petitioners put to lot of mental agony, untold misery and lost earning member of the family.
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the respondents.

sentences.text: The notice of the petition has been duly served on Respondent No.1 and 2.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before this Tribunal.
Hence, Respondent No.1 has been placed exparte.
5. The Respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed its written statement denying the entire petition averments as false and baseless.
The Respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed his written statement denying the issuance of insurance policy with respect to car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058.
Further he has contended that his liability is limited subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further he has denied the age, income of the deceased at the time of accident.
He has also denied that the accident occurred only due to rash and SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.3272/2020 negligent act of car and not due to the negligence of deceased.
He has further contended that the owner of the car and the police have not complied with mandatory provisions after the alleged accident.
If this tribunal pleases to pass an award, the rate of interest may be restricted to 6% per annum.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings of both the parties, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased B.N.Kemparaju S/o.

Hanumanthaiah, aged about 28 years, was dies in a road traffic accident that occurred on 24.08.2020 at about 4.00 pm., while deceased was riding on his Honda Shine Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-L-6060, when he reached on Tumkur-Bangalore NH-48 Road, near billinakote,
Sompura hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the Toyota Innova Car bearing No.KA-51-Z-5058 drove in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle.
As a result deceased sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in claim petition ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent ?
SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.3272/2020 3.
What order or award?

8.

 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

 REASONS  10. ISSUE NO.1:

As already stated supra, it is the  SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.3272/2020 case of PW.1 that on 24.08.2020 at about 4.00 pm., when her deceased husband was riding his Honda Shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-L-6060 from Dabaspete to Nelamangala on Tumkur-Bangalore NH-48 on the Billinakote bridge slowly, carefully by observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time, a Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life while crossing the divider and dashed to her deceased husband's motor cycle.
Due to the impact, her deceased husband fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately her deceased husband was taken to Swastya Hospital, Nelamangala and in the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 29.08.2020.
11.
On the other hand, it is the contention of Respondent No.2 that the insured vehicle has been implicated in collusion with concerned persons to get wrongful gain to the petitioners.

Therefore,
the burden is on the petitioners to prove the actionable negligence on the part of driver of the offending Car.
As already stated supra SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.3272/2020 the Petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW.2.

She has filed affidavit for her chief examination and re-iterated the entire petition averments and she adopt the earlier marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.18.
12.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint lodged by one of the injured person in the alleged accident, the Nelamangala police have registered FIR in Crime No.299/2020 against the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058 for the offenses punishable u/s.279, 337 of IPC.
After due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Car for the offenses punishable u/s.338, 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.6 is the spot sketch and it shows that the accident took place at Tumkur - Bangalore NH-47 road.
The IMV report marked at Ex.P.7 which shows that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P.3 is the post mortem report and Ex.P.4 is the inquest report of the deceased.
As per these documents the deceased died due to injury to the brain.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.3272/2020 examined PW.2 but he has failed to elicit anything from her to disbelieve her version.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective.
13. On the other hand the MRO at Swasthya Hospital, Bengaluru has examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to R.4 and the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer as RW.2.
He has filed affidavit for his examination in chief.

He has produced policy copy at authorization Usharani N.C vs Savithiri on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54923058/
4 letter and insurance policy at Ex.R.5 and 6 respectively.
He has denied the issuance of policy in favour of first respondent in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51- Z-5058 and also denied the insured and insurer relationship.
He has also deposed that as per medical records it shows the first respondent car was not caused alleged accident and it is created by the petitioners.
He has produced policy of Insurance at Ex.R.6.

In his cross- examination the RW.2 has admitted that,

14.
Therefore, in my opinion, though the Respondent No.2 has taken up defense, but he has failed to prove the same.
Therefore, from the evidence of both the parties it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Z-5058 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2: PW.1 has produced Aadhar cards of deceased, Petitioners No.2 to 4 and of herself which are SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.3272/2020 marked at Ex.P.9 to 12 and also produced Ration card at Ex.14.
From these documents it is clear that petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is minor daughter and petitioners No.3 and 4 are aged parents of deceased.
Therefore, they are considered as legal heirs of deceased.
16. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:- PW.2 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.13.
As per this document he was born on 08.12.1989.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was 31 years.

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '16'.
17.

In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.3272/2020 tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.

As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Usharani N.C vs Savithiri on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54923058/

sentences.text: The deceased was aged about 31 years as on the date of accident and his income is taken into consideration as Rs.14,500/-p.m.
As per the Hon'ble Apex court reported in a decision reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others),

entities.text: (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects as the deceased was below 40 years.
Therefore, 40% of Rs.14,500/- works out to Rs.5,800/-.
Therefore, the total income of the deceased works out to Rs.20,300/- (Rs.14,500/-+ Rs.5,800/-).
Since the petitioners No.1 to 4 are the dependents of the deceased, the 1/4 th of the total salary is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, 1/4th of Rs.20,300/- works out to Rs.5,075/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.15,225/- (20,300/- (-) 5,075/-).

Annual income works out to Rs.1,82,700/- (15,225/- x 12).
SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.3272/2020 Appropriate multiplier is "16".
Thus loss of dependency works-out to Rs.29,23,200/- (1,82,700/- x 16).

19. Further, as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others, amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years under the following conventional heads.

20. As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018D.D.18.09/2018) the petitioner No.2 being the child of the deceased is awarded Rs.44,000/- under the head of Loss of parental consortium and petitioner No.3 and 4 being the parents are awarded Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Loss of filial consortium.

sentences.text: 21. PW.2 has produced medical bills at Ex.P.15.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioners have spent Rs.4,10,800/- towards medical expenses of SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.3272/2020 deceased.
The medical bills appear to be genuine in the absence of challenge.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.4,10,800/- towards Medical Expenses.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :-
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 29,23,200=00 2 Loss of consortium to Rs. 44,000=00 petitioner No.1 3 Loss of parental Rs. 44,000=00 consortium to petitioner No.2 4 Loss of filial consortium Rs. 88,000=00 (44,000x2) 5 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500=00 6
Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500=00 7
Medical Expenses Rs. 4,10,800=00 GRAND TOTAL Rs. 35,43,000=00
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,43,000/-.
23. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

Usharani N.C vs Savithiri on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54923058/
6 SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.3272/2020 24.

The respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending Car and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending vehicle and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was having valid insurance policy.

Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'Partly affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,43,000/- (Rupees Thirty five Lakhs forty-three thousand only) SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.3272/2020 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Car is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

On deposit of the award amount  together with interest, the claimants are  entitled for the compensation amount by  way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 60%
 Petitioner No.2 - 30%
 Petitioner No.3&4 - 5% each Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1
a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her on verification.
However the said Petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

Entire compensation amount of  SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.3272/2020 Usharani N.C vs Savithiri on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54923058/
7 petitioner No.2 shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized bank of petitioner No.1's choice till she attains the age of majority.
Entire compensation amount of petitioner No.3 and 4 shall be released to them on verification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.
